Neha —

Quick notes after skimming both proposals and the comparison sheet:

- Cost: Kite appears ~25% more expensive on the surface but includes a bundled ISO27001 add-on that might be cheaper than separate engagements. Eversend's quote is leaner but has hourly add-ons for reporting and remediation support.
- Timeline: Kite can commit to a mid-Oct testing window and finish both attestations by end-Nov. Eversend proposes a later kickoff (late Oct) and may push the report to mid-Dec if scope is expanded.
- Evidence handling: Kite uses an encrypted ShareFile instance (meets our KMS requirement). Eversend wants us to use our S3 bucket with presigned links — that's ok but legal will want stricter access logs.
- References: I called two startups that used Kite last year — consistent quality and good responsiveness during remediation. Eversend has more enterprise references but a mixed timeline record.

I flagged three procurement items: SLAs on report delivery, audit staff substitution clause (we need notice & replacement commitment), and liability cap relative to professional fees. I'll add those to the comparison tab.

Attached: excerpt from Kite_Proposal_Redwood_2026.pdf (price table) — see highlighted lines in sheet.

—Aditya

Subject: Fwd: Eversend SOW (redlines)

Neha — forwarding my procurement/legal redlines on Eversend (see Eversend_SOW_draft.docx). Major points:

- Replace their proposed 30-day invoice term with net 45 for our standard flow.
- Add a clause requiring encrypted transfer + immutable access logs for evidence uploads; vendor must provide monthly access logs.
- Professional liability cap: ask for negotiation to 2x fees for gross negligence (current clause is too broad).
- Require a 30-day remediation period before termination for non-material breaches.

If we select Kite, we should run the same redline list against their SOW; their proposal looks more mature from a contractual standpoint but we should still push on liability and SLAs.

Team —

Thanks for the quick reviews. After weighing timeline risk vs. bundled cost and reference checks, my recommendation: engage Kite Consulting as primary vendor, with Eversend as fallback if contract or timing cannot be agreed. Rationale in brief:

- Kite commits to the Oct testing window and delivers both SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 in a contiguous engagement, which materially reduces program risk.
- Their evidence handling meets our KMS/encryption needs out of the box.
- Higher sticker price is offset by a faster timeline and fewer add-ons; expected delta is ~$35k (see audit_comparison.xlsx).

Ask:
- Laura / Procurement: start SOW negotiations with Kite tomorrow (8/26) and apply the redline checklist in my earlier email + your list.
- Aditya: can you confirm any infra-specific scoped items that must be added to the SOW (e.g., access to prefixed logs, KV cache traces)? Need this by 8/26 noon.
- Monica: please schedule a vendor scoping call (Kite and Eversend) for 8/27–8/28; include Compliance, Product Infra, and Procurement.

If no objections by EOD 8/26 I'll instruct procurement to issue an LOI and get signatures. Attaching links: AUD-117 (Jira) and proposal notes (https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xProposalNotesRedwood).

Thanks —
